nodes.name: Webhook: Manual Upload
nodes.notes: Entry point A. The Next.js app POSTs the syllabus here as multipart/form-data under the field name `syllabus`. Header auth means an unauthenticated caller on port 5678 cannot inject calendar events.

nodes.name: Drive: New Syllabus Dropped
nodes.notes: Entry point B — the zero-effort path. Watches one Drive folder; dropping a syllabus in it runs the whole pipeline with no UI interaction at all. Ships DISABLED because n8n refuses to activate a workflow whose trigger has no credential — that would block the upload path too. Connect Google Drive, set the folder, then enable this node.

nodes.name: Drive: Download File
nodes.notes: Scope is drive.readonly — this pipeline never writes to or deletes from Drive.

nodes.name: Find the Uploaded File
nodes.notes: Both entry points feed through here so the rest of the pipeline can rely on the file being at `syllabus` regardless of how it arrived.

nodes.name: Extract Text from PDF
nodes.notes: Text extraction happens locally inside the container. Only the extracted text — never the raw file — is sent to any external API.

nodes.name: Claude: Extract Schedule + Costs
nodes.notes: claude-opus-5 with adaptive thinking and a strict json_schema output contract. The API key lives in n8n's encrypted credential store, never in the workflow JSON.

nodes.name: Any Events to Add?
nodes.notes: A syllabus with no resolvable dates is a legitimate outcome. Without this branch the empty SplitOut would stall the pipeline and the webhook would time out with no answer.

nodes.name: Google Calendar: Create Event
nodes.notes: Point this at a dedicated calendar rather than `primary` for a safer demo — a bad extraction then pollutes one throwaway calendar instead of the student's real one. onError=continue so one rejected event does not abort the whole import.
